clue.text: Old party officer heads band of soldiers

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun: one who heads a military band

parts.note: a drum was an 18th-century word for a crowded evening party or rout
a major is an army officer

explanation.surface: A veteran political officer leads a troop of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old party' suggests a political party; it is the obsolete social sense of drum, a fashionable gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: The noncommissioned officer who marches in front of a military band, twirling a mace, leads it.

clue.text: Lines of bishops

parts.note: read as chess: the slanting paths along which a chess bishop moves

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests lines of descent of clergy; in chess a bishop only ever moves on the slant.
explanation.definitionFit: Slanting lines across a board are exactly the routes a chess bishop may travel.

clue.text: They employ topless nurses smashing!

indicators.note: smashing breaks up the remaining letters and rearranges them
the word nurses loses its top, that is its first letter

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at nurses without their tops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes N from NURSES, leaving URSES, which 'smashing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: People who employ something are those who make use of it.

clue.text: Swimmer- Dick. swallows one litre vermouth-essential for speed

indicators.note: the whale's name takes the other pieces inside it, as a whale swallows

parts.note: Moby Dick, the swimming white whale of Melville's novel, gives its first name
one is the Roman numeral I
IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A whale swallows a litre of vermouth, which somehow helps it go fast.
explanation.walkthrough: IT, short for Italian vermouth, is an old British bar order ('gin and it').
explanation.definitionFit: The capacity to move freely is a prerequisite for going fast.

clue.text: Raise bottle, nothing in it. One used to get a kick from it

definitions.text: One used to get a kick from it

parts.note: to jack something is to raise it, as with a car jack

indicators.note: the zero is placed inside the abbreviation for bottle

parts.note: BOT is the abbreviation for bottle
O is the zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Lift an empty bottle; someone used to get a kick out of drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The kick looks like a drinker's thrill; it is a literal kick from a heavy military boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy military boot reaching the knee was literally the thing a soldier kicked with.

clue.text: Decline rubbish

definitions.meaning: to decline is to say no to something

explanation.definitionFit: Stressed on the second syllable it means turn down; stressed on the first it means waste matter.

clue.text: Witch's. contribution to Ruddigore

parts.note: the plot of the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta Ruddigore turns on a witch's spell laid on the baronets

explanation.walkthrough: In Ruddigore a witch, burned at the stake, dooms every Baronet of Ruddigore to commit a crime daily or die.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch's malediction on the family drives the whole plot of that operetta.

clue.text: Cavalier leader en route for Welsh, port

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: en route means on the way, travelling

explanation.surface: A Royalist commander is heading for a harbour in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Cavaliers were the Royalists of the English Civil War, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: The town on the north Wales coast with its castle and harbour is a port.

clue.text: Precipitation is affected by gravity -

parts.note: read as a statement about wet weather: rain falls because of gravity

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like physics or chemistry, where precipitation means a solid settling out; read it as weather and the falling rain is what is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Drops of rain are the falling water that makes up precipitation.

clue.text: Poor Tom can make the grade

indicators.note: the letters of grade can be made into a new word

explanation.surface: A struggling boy named Tom manages to pass.
explanation.walkthrough: In King Lear, Edgar disguises himself as the mad beggar 'Poor Tom'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloucester's son in King Lear goes about disguised as the beggar Poor Tom.

clue.text: Still, a bit old-fashioned

parts.note: Still reads as an adverb but is the noun, distilling apparatus of an antique kind

explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' seems to mean 'even so'; it is a distilling still, and the answer is the alchemist's old type.
explanation.definitionFit: The alchemists' distilling vessel with a beaked cap is an outdated form of still.

clue.text: Swordplay keeps us within bounds

definitions.meaning: the sport of fighting with foils, épées or sabres
a barrier of posts and rails encloses land and keeps people in

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the sport with swords and the railings that enclose a field.

clue.text: No use looking here for a bird!

indicators.note: here points to the run of letters inside the words No use looking

explanation.surface: Don't bother searching this spot for a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'nO USE Looking'. It is an old spelling of ouzel, the blackbird.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for the blackbird or the ring ouzel, a thrush.

clue.text: Brown Derby's partly back … to front, he observes

indicators.note: Derby's is split into parts so that the colour can go between them
the front of the word is moved round to its back

parts.note: the word Derby's taken letter for letter, with its S
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: Someone watches a brown bowler hat being turned around.
explanation.walkthrough: A brown derby is an American name for a bowler hat, so the surface pictures a hat being turned round; 'back to front' and 'partly' both work on the racecourse name instead.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker is someone who watches without taking part.

clue.text: Test player for instance

parts.note: not a cricketer in a Test match but a trial of a performer's skill

explanation.walkthrough: 'Test player' suggests an international cricketer; read 'Test' as a verb and it is a trial performance, given for example by an actor or musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial performance by which an actor or musician is judged for a part.

clue.text: Scottish schoolman in one scene in Shakespeare

parts.note: Duns Scotus was a Scottish scholastic philosopher, a schoolman
ane is the Scots word for one

explanation.surface: A Scots scholar appears in a scene of a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: Schoolmen were the medieval scholastic philosophers; John Duns Scotus is the best known Scot among them.
explanation.definitionFit: The castle hill in Macbeth where the final act's battle takes place is a setting in that play.

clue.text: Titania's attendant wasn't the tiger type '

definitions.text: Titania's attendant wasn't the tiger type '

parts.words: Titania's attendant wasn't the tiger type '
parts.note: one of the fairy queen's attendants in A Midsummer Night's Dream, plus a joke on the tiger species of the insect

explanation.walkthrough: Titania's fairies include Peaseblossom, Cobweb, Mustardseed and one named after an insect; the tiger is a common species of that insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy serving Titania in A Midsummer Night's Dream bears the name of a winged insect.

clue.text: Proverbially a lost cause?

parts.note: the proverb says he who wavers is lost, so the wavering is what causes the loss

explanation.walkthrough: 'A lost cause' looks like a hopeless venture; read as the cause of being lost, the proverb 'he who hesitates is lost' supplies it.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb makes indecision the thing that leads to being lost.

clue.text: Inferior numbers

parts.note: numbers is an old word for verses, so this is bad poetry

explanation.walkthrough: 'Numbers' suggests arithmetic or minorities; in poetry numbers are metrical lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Badly written comic verse is poetry of poor quality.

clue.text: It 'may be caused by a bone of contention

definitions.text: It 'may be caused by a bone of contention

parts.words: It 'may be caused by a bone of contention
parts.note: a bone of contention is usually a dispute; here a real bone two hounds fight over

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'bone of contention' is taken literally: two hounds tussling over a real bone.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap between animals over a bone is literally a canine fight.

clue.text: Emulate bird.(which Americans do in it twice)

definitions.text: Emulate bird.(which Americans do in it twice)

parts.words: Emulate bird.(which Americans do in it twice)
parts.note: copy a songbird; the bracket hints at the New York prison whose name doubles the word, where Americans do time

explanation.walkthrough: Sing Sing is a famous New York state prison; to 'do bird' is British slang for serving a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Making music with the voice copies what a songbird does.

clue.text: Giant keeps souls in torment in a Greek island

indicators.note: the tormented letters are placed inside the island's name

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese

indicators.note: souls in torment are twisted, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A giant holds tormented souls captive on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: The most famous Colossus stood on Rhodes, so a Greek island feels natural in the surface; Cos is a different island, used only as the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge statue such as the one at Rhodes gives its name to anything gigantic.

clue.text: People among whom I name a dramatist

indicators.note: the people take the other letters into their midst

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Among a group of people I name one as a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text shows '2' where the page prints 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Racine was a French tragic playwright of the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Adam and Eve up in the wood moving to 14

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Adam was the first man
Eve was made from Adam's rib

explanation.surface: The first couple climb in the forest that marches on the castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MAN plus RIB backwards. 14 is DUNSINANE: in Macbeth, Birnam Wood comes to Dunsinane.
explanation.definitionFit: In Macbeth the soldiers carry boughs from this forest towards the castle, fulfilling the prophecy.

clue.text: Exercising one's copyright ?

parts.note: copyright read as the right to copy, so using it means copying

explanation.walkthrough: Copyright is normally the right to stop copying; split it as 'copy right' and exercising it is copying.
explanation.definitionFit: Copying someone is acting on a supposed right to copy.

clue.text: Members of a Worshipful Company.?.

parts.note: a Worshipful Company is a London livery guild; read literally, it is a group of things worshipped

explanation.walkthrough: London's livery companies (guilds) carry the title 'Worshipful'; read literally, worshipful company is a set of worshipped images.
explanation.definitionFit: Images or false gods are objects of worship.

clue.text: Ostensible, purpose, of the battle-line

definitions.meaning: an outward show that hides the real aim
the foremost line where armies meet

explanation.definitionFit: A cover operation hiding the real business, and the forward line of fighting in a war.

clue.text: The sultan a 20.?.

definitions.meaning: ... I founded the Ottoman dynasty of sultans
20 is COLOSSUS: a giant read as OS (outsize) plus MAN

explanation.walkthrough: OS is the abbreviation for outsize on clothing labels.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Ottoman ruler, and a giant fellow split as outsize plus man.

clue.text: Antony made one, though implying, he couldn't

definitions.text: Antony made one, though implying, he couldn't

parts.words: Antony made one, though implying, he couldn't
parts.note: in Julius Caesar Mark Antony gives a famous funeral speech while saying 'I am no orator, as Brutus is'

explanation.walkthrough: Antony's 'Friends, Romans, countrymen' speech contains his claim to be no speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal public speech, as Antony gives over Caesar's body.

clue.text: Rule, mostly that of Knox's women

indicators.note: mostly means the word is used all but its last letter

parts.note: John Knox wrote The First Blast of the Trumpet against the Monstrous Regiment of Women

explanation.surface: A rule that applies mostly to Knox's women.
explanation.walkthrough: Knox's 'regiment' meant rule; dropping its last letter gives a modern word for a regime of diet or exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A prescribed course of diet or exercise is a set of rules to follow.

clue.text: The kid's taken a nap

parts.note: the child seems to be sleeping; really kid leather has had a napped finish raised on it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child and 'nap' a sleep; kid is goatskin leather, and nap is a raised fibrous surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather, often kid, with the flesh side buffed to a velvety nap.

clue.text: Characteristic 'of 'a:'church of Christian soldiers

parts.note: the Church Militant is the church on earth, and 'Onward, Christian Soldiers' marches as to war

explanation.walkthrough: The Church Militant is the theological term for Christians living on earth, fighting evil.
explanation.definitionFit: A warlike, combative quality is what marks a fighting church.
